# rebuild_hash_sidecars

[← Command index](README.md)

Rebuild a remote locker's hash sidecar database from local content.

## Synopsis

```
rebuild_hash_sidecars [options]
```

## Description

The hash sidecar is a SQLite database, `.locker_hashes.db`, at the root of a remote
locker. It records the path, MD5, size and modification time of each file as it is on
the local side (before any encryption). Remotes that cannot hash files themselves,
such as the SFTP-based Hetzner locker, rely on it: `locker_sync_tool` and
`master_backup` read it instead of asking the remote, so it has to be current for
their comparisons to be right.

The tool downloads the existing database if there is one, hashes the source locker's
files (or the `--path` subtree), writes the new entries over any existing ones for the
same paths, and uploads the database back to the destination locker's root. Hidden
directories and the destination locker's configured `excluded_dirs` are skipped.
Directories with more than 500 files or 10 GB are hashed one at a time first; the
rest are hashed `--parallel_dirs` at a time.

`--skip_existing` is keyed on path, not content: a file that already has an entry
keeps its old row even if the file has changed. Every file is still hashed; only the
database write is skipped. Use it to add new files quickly, and run without it when
files may have changed. If the existing database cannot be downloaded, the run
starts from an empty one, so nothing is skipped.

## Options

### Lockers

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-l, --source_locker <source_locker>` | Locker whose mount path holds the files to hash. Default: `Local`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `-d, --dest_locker <dest_locker>` | Remote locker whose `.locker_hashes.db` is rebuilt; must be a configured rclone remote. Default: `Hetzner`. Allowed: `All`, `Local`, `Hetzner`, `Gdrive`, `External`. |
| `--path <path>` | Subtree relative to the locker root to rehash, e.g. `Gaming/Roms`; the whole locker when empty. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-c, --clear` | Delete the existing database at the destination root before rebuilding. |
| `-s, --skip_existing` | Leave existing database entries untouched and add only paths that have none. |
| `-r, --parallel_dirs <parallel_dirs>` | Number of directories hashed at the same time. Default: `4`. |
| `-f, --parallel_files <parallel_files>` | Number of files hashed at the same time within each directory. Default: `4`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Rebuild the Hetzner sidecar from the local locker

```bash
rebuild_hash_sidecars -l Local -d Hetzner -v
```

### Show what would be hashed without uploading anything

```bash
rebuild_hash_sidecars -p -v
```

### Add entries only for files not yet in the database

```bash
rebuild_hash_sidecars -s -v
```

### Rehash one subtree

```bash
rebuild_hash_sidecars --path "Gaming/Roms" -v
```

### Start from an empty database and rehash the whole locker

```bash
rebuild_hash_sidecars -c -v
```

## Notes

- Entries for files that were deleted locally stay in the database until it is rebuilt with `-c`.
- `-c` deletes the whole database at the destination root, even when `--path` limits the rehash to a subtree, so combine them only when you mean to drop every other entry.
- Peak memory is about `parallel_dirs` x `parallel_files` x the hashing chunk size; the preview shows the figure.
- Hetzner's SFTP shell has no usable `md5sum`, so an rclone remote with `md5sum_command` set fails to verify the upload, reports `corrupted on transfer`, and deletes the uploaded database. Set `disable_hashcheck = true` on that remote and remove any `md5sum_command`/`sha1sum_command`; the Hetzner template in the rclone setup already does this.
- `master_backup` refreshes the sidecar after each backup, so this tool is mainly for repairs and first-time setup.
